videos.script: Appium drives an app from outside. Espresso lives inside it. {{inside}} An Espresso test is packed into a second APK and installed beside the app. It runs in the app's own process, so it can reach the app's views directly. {{process}} That makes it fast, and it makes it patient. Before every step, Espresso waits until the app's main thread has nothing left to do. {{sync}} But only the main thread. Tickets loads its shows on a thread of its own, and Espresso cannot see it. A test that taps the list too early fails now and then. Nothing on the screen says why. {{race}} So in this lesson you write the tests for Tickets in Kotlin. Then you teach Espresso to wait for the load. {{idling}} Then a test of the offline banner. It needs boxoffice to be unreachable on purpose. {{offline}} And last, how these tests are run, by Android Studio or by Gradle, and where their report lands. {{run}}
